INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 40.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper. questions.questionText: A desk has a true width of 50.0cm. Two students, X and Y, measure the width of the desk. Student X uses a tape measure and records a width of (49.5  0.5)cm. Student Y uses a metre rule and records a width of (51.4  0.1)cm. Which statement about the measurement of student X is correct?

options.A: It is less accurate and less precise than the measurement of student Y.
options.B: It is less accurate but more precise than the measurement of student Y.
options.C: It is more accurate and more precise than the measurement of student Y.
options.D: It is more accurate but less precise than the measurement of student Y.

questions.questionText: A device for spraying paint consists of a box with its faces horizontal and vertical. One of its vertical faces contains small holes. The density of the paint is 900kgm–3. What is the horizontal force required to hold the device stationary as it ejects the paint?

questions.questionText: Two balls of identical shape and size but different masses are falling through the same liquid. The sum of the drag force and upthrust acting on each ball is equal to its weight. Which statement about the two balls is correct?

options.A: The heavier ball has a larger acceleration than the lighter ball.
options.B: The heavier ball has a smaller deceleration than the lighter ball.
options.C: The heavier ball is falling at the same speed as the lighter ball.
options.D: The heavier ball is falling at a larger speed than the lighter ball.

Object X travels at speed v before the collision and speed in the opposite direction after the collision. Object Y is stationary before the collision. 3v v X Y X Y m 4m m 4m before after What is the kinetic energy of Y after the collision?
What is not a requirement for two forces to act as a couple?

options.A: The two forces act in opposite directions.
options.B: The two forces act through the same point.
options.C: The two forces combine to produce zero resultant force.
options.D: The two forces have equal magnitude.

questions.questionText: An airport has a mechanical system for moving luggage. The system uses a horizontal conveyor belt, a sloping conveyor belt, a lift and a frictionless slide. A suitcase is moved around the airport using this system.
m Resistive forces opposing the motion of the suitcase are negligible. For which movement of the suitcase is the net work done on the suitcase greatest?

options.A: moving the suitcase a distance of 8m at a constant speed up the sloping conveyor belt
options.B: moving the suitcase a distance of 16m at a constant speed along the horizontal conveyor belt
options.C: moving the suitcase a distance of 10m at a constant speed vertically upwards on the lift
options.D: moving the suitcase a distance of 12m at increasing speed downwards on the slide

An experiment is set up to demonstrate the diffraction of water waves in a ripple tank. The waves pass through a gap of width w and some diffraction of the waves is observed. The wavelength of the waves is now doubled. What is the new gap width needed to cause the same amount of diffraction as before?
Two coherent electromagnetic waves are travelling in a vacuum. The two waves meet at a point. At this point, the two waves have different intensities. Which statement about the waves is not correct?

options.A: They have a constant phase difference at the point.
options.B: They have the same amplitude at the point.
options.D: They travel at the same speed.

options.C: Positively charged electrons in the wire move from the positive terminal to the negative terminal.
options.D: Positively charged nuclei in the wire move from the positive terminal to the negative terminal.
